PROJECT 02

DirtLENS

Overview

A handheld soil-color recognition tool designed to make field classification faster and more consistent by controlling capture, illumination, analysis, and display in one device.

RoleProduct / UX/UI / Python
PlatformEmbedded Hardware
StackPython / OpenCV / Raspberry Pi
StatusWorking Prototype

Problem

Color by eye varies

Soil color is useful field data, but ambient light, viewing conditions, and individual interpretation can change the recorded result.

Response

Control the variables

DirtLENS combines the camera, illumination, reading area, analysis, and display into one device so every reading follows the same sequence.

Workflow

Four linked steps

The physical product and software are designed as one instrument rather than separate hardware and interface layers.

01 / Challenge

The field problem and the product response

Soil color is useful field data, but visual comparison can change with lighting, viewing conditions, and the person making the observation. DirtLENS treats those variables as a product-design problem.

Existing workflow

Color by eye

Field classification depends on visual comparison and ambient conditions. That introduces variation into a task that is expected to be recorded consistently across people, sites, and days.

DirtLENS response

Control the reading

The device combines a camera, fixed reading area, controlled LED ring, image analysis, and an on-device display so the user follows one repeatable capture sequence instead of making a freehand visual judgment.

Audience

Archaeologists and field researchers recording soil data.

My contribution

Product concept, UX/UI, Python, computer vision, hardware integration.

Core constraint

Lighting, camera position, and reading area have to remain controlled.

Current state

Integrated Raspberry Pi prototype with live camera, illumination, and display.
02 / System

One short interaction, four linked systems

The interface is intentionally small because most of the design work happens before the result appears: the physical chamber, lighting, camera, and software all have to produce the same kind of reading each time.

01
Illuminate

A fixed LED ring supplies the sample with controlled light inside the device.

02
Capture

The camera reads a defined circular region rather than the entire frame.

03
Analyze

Python and OpenCV process the selected area and classify the observed soil color.

04
Display

The result is returned directly on the device display for field use.

03 / Build

The interface is part of the instrument

DirtLENS is not a screen-first product. The physical layout, enclosure, illumination, camera, software, and display form one interface.

01

Fixed ROI

The software samples a defined circular region so surrounding material and background do not dominate the color reading.

02

Controlled light

The LED ring is positioned as part of the optical system rather than treated as an external accessory.

03

Immediate feedback

The rear display shows the live camera view and resulting information without requiring a laptop or separate phone.

“The goal is not to make the user better at judging color. It is to remove as much judgment from the measurement as possible.”
04 / Current Outcome

A working integrated prototype

The current device combines the core hardware and software into a single field unit. The next work is refinement and validation rather than proving that the basic interaction can function.
